  Urban agriculture is promoted as a climate-smart lever for food security, yet its spatial pattern and local food-security linkage remain under-quantified in Nigeria. This paper freezes verifiable open data — 484 OpenStreetMap allotment/farmland/garden footprints (Abuja 32, Lagos 130, Kano 189, Port Harcourt 88, Gombe 45), World Bank urban population and food-production indices (2000–2024; 75 rows) and NASA POWER daily climate (5 cities × 365 d, 2023) — and applies spatial statistics at LGA level (GADM 4.1, 775 LGAs). # Introduction

Urban agriculture in Nigerian cities — encompassing dry-season fadama along riverbeds, irrigated peri-urban farmland, and intra-urban allotments — is increasingly positioned as a climate-smart lever for food security and community resilience amid accelerated urbanisation and climate variability [@orhevba2024; @faostat2024; @abubakar2023; @fao2023]. Nigeria's urban population reached 146.5 million in 2024 (>55% of the total) [@worldbank2024; @undesa2022], outpacing formal food-system infrastructure and creating a pressing need to map where urban agriculture occurs and whether its concentration aligns with food-security needs [@udoh2022; @frayne2014; @ogundele2023].

Evidence remains fragmented and aspatial: surveys rarely georeference sites, case studies seldom formalise dependence, and food-security metrics mask intra-urban heterogeneity [@zezza2010; @aubry2012; @adeleye2024], limiting translation into zoning, fadama protection and compost loops (sub-themes 6/10/13). The National Urban Policy (2022) prioritises compact cities and food-system integration but lacks LGA-level evidence — a gap addressed here.

We address this by (i) freezing OSM and indicator footprints with provenance (16 entries) [@openstreetmap2024; @nasapower2024], (ii) applying Moran/LISA and lag/error regression (Eqs. @eq-moran–@eq-error, `sf`/`spdep`/`terra`) [@pebesma2023; @bivand2023; @anselin1995; @moran1950], and (iii) translating clusters ($I=0.300$, $p<0.001$) into zoning and circular-system insights.

# Study Area and Data

## Study Area

Five cities maximise agro-ecological and urban-form variation: Abuja (planned capital, Guinean savanna), Lagos (coastal megacity), Kano (Sahelian), Port Harcourt (humid Niger Delta) and Gombe (savanna, host region). They span 404–1,891 mm rainfall and 25.9–27.3°C (Table 2), affording a gradient for H2. The LGA (GADM v4.1, 775 units) is the areal unit, balancing administrative relevance for zoning with globally-available boundaries [@gadm2022].

## Data (frozen via APIs, provenance in `data/raw/provenance.json`)

Data were acquired via one-time scripted queries (`ds-general` Python 3.12) and frozen to `data/raw/*.csv` with `provenance.json` (16 entries, URL/timestamp/licence) ensuring reproducibility without further network calls.

| Layer | Source | Endpoint | Retained | $n$ |
|---|---|---|---|---:|
| Urban-ag footprints | OSM Overpass | `https://overpass-api.de/api/interpreter` | `landuse` allotments/farmland/farmyard, `leisure` garden (dedup. `type+id`) | 484 |
| Population/food | World Bank WDI | `.../NG/indicator/{SP.URB.TOTL,AG.PRD.FOOD.XD,SN.ITK.DEFC.ZS}` | Pop., food index, undernourishment % | 75 |
| Climate | NASA POWER AG | `.../power.larc.nasa.gov/api/temporal/daily/point?community=AG` | T2M, PRECTOTCORR, RH2M (daily 2023) | 1,825 |
| Boundaries | GADM v4.1 | `.../gadm41_NGA_shp.zip` | LGA polygons | 775 |
| Food stub | FAOSTAT | `.../faostat/api/v1/en/data/FS` → 521 → stub | `fao_food_security.csv` | 1 |

FAOSTAT 521 → 1-row stub retained (see `data/external/README.md`). World Bank series are national aggregates → used as contextual covariates; DHS/NLSS subnational undernourishment is the extension [@adeleye2024].

# Methods

## Design and hypotheses

We adopt a non-experimental spatial-observational design appropriate for areal inference from open data [@bivand2023; @pebesma2023]. Nigeria's agro-ecological gradient — from arid Sahel (Kano 404 mm) to humid delta (Port Harcourt 1,891 mm) — motivates three pre-registered hypotheses [@muhammed2022; @arowolo2023; @ogundele2023]. H1 posits that urban-agriculture density is spatially clustered, implying $I>0$ in Eq. @eq-moran and warranting spatial rather than ordinary regression. H2 posits that density increases with aridity: lower annual precipitation and higher temperature enhance the relative value of irrigated fadama and therefore allotment intensity. H3 posits a scale effect: density declines with LGA area because larger administrative units dilute point intensity, implying a negative coefficient on $\log(\text{area})$ in Eqs. @eq-lag–@eq-error.

## Spatial descriptive

Density $=n/\text{area}_{km^2}$ with $\text{area}_{km^2}=\text{st\_area}/10^6$ (`sf` GEOS) corrects ten-fold LGA variation (11.6–10,358 km², median 697 km²); $I$ rises 0.158→0.300 upon normalisation (§Results). Kernel/G(r) omitted for page limit.

## Spatial dependence — formal tests

Let $\mathbf{x} = (x_1,\dots,x_N)^\top$ be density (or counts) on $N=775$ LGAs, $\bar{x}$ its mean, $m_2 = N^{-1}\sum_i (x_i-\bar{x})^2$, and $\mathbf{W}=[w_{ij}]$ the queen contiguity matrix row-standardised.

**Weight matrix** (Eq. @eq-w):

$$
w_{ij} = \begin{cases}1 &\text{if LGAs } i,j \text{ share edge or vertex}\\0 &\text{otherwise}\end{cases}, \qquad w^*_{ij}=w_{ij}/\sum_j w_{ij} \tag{1}
$$ {#eq-w}

Queen versus rook $\mathbf{W}$ yields $I_{density}=0.300$ versus $0.306$ (both $z>17.5$, $p<0.001$), confirming robustness to diagonal neighbours.

**Global Moran's I** [@moran1950; @cliff1981] (Eq. @eq-moran):

$$
I = \frac{N}{W}\frac{\sum_i\sum_j w^*_{ij}(x_i-\bar{x})(x_j-\bar{x})}{\sum_i (x_i-\bar{x})^2},\quad E[I]=-\tfrac{1}{N-1},\quad z=\tfrac{I-E[I]}{\sqrt{\text{Var}[I]}} \tag{2}
$$ {#eq-moran}

Tested with `spdep::moran.test` (randomisation, `zero.policy=TRUE`) and variance under randomisation. Rejection ($p<0.001$) implies clustering beyond complete spatial randomness (CSR) and motivates spatial regression [@anselin1995; @bivand2022] (see Eq. @eq-lag and Eq. @eq-error).

**LISA** (Local Moran, Eq. @eq-lisa):

$$
I_i = \frac{x_i-\bar{x}}{m_2}\sum_j w^*_{ij}(x_j-\bar{x}) \tag{3}
$$ {#eq-lisa}

`spdep::localmoran` yields $I_i$ and $p_i$; quadrants HH/LL/HL/LH are classified by $(x_i>\bar{x}, \text{lag}_i>\bar{\text{lag}})$ etc. only when $p_i<0.05$, mapping Eq. @eq-lisa to HH/LL clusters in Fig. @fig-lisa.

## Spatial regression

Conditional on H1, OLS is biased (residuals remain spatially autocorrelated, violating Gauss–Markov). We therefore specify lag and error models (`spatialreg` 1.4.3 [@bivand2023]) for comparison:

$$
y = \rho \mathbf{W} y + X\beta + \varepsilon \tag{4}
$$ {#eq-lag}

Eq. @eq-lag is the spatial lag (spillover: neighbours' $y$ directly affects $y$).

$$
y = X\beta + u,\; u = \lambda \mathbf{W} u + \varepsilon,\; \varepsilon\sim N(0,\sigma^2 I) \tag{5}
$$ {#eq-error}

Eq. @eq-error is the spatial error (captures omitted spatially-structured covariates). Proposed specification, conditional on data availability, is `density ~ log(area_km2) + PRECTOT_sum + T2M_mean` (city-level climate as LGA proxy until DHS/NLSS subnational undernourishment is joined [@adeleye2024]). Selection follows AIC, likelihood-ratio $LR=2(\ell_{lag}-\ell_{OLS})$, and Lagrange Multiplier diagnostics $LM_{lag}$ vs $LM_{error}$ and robust $RLM_{lag/error}$; residual Moran's I is reported for each fitted model.

## Suitability overlay

Suitability overlay (`terra` 1.7 [@hijmans2023; @anand2021]) on market/water proximity and unbuilt land will prioritise HH LGAs (Eq. @eq-lisa) — staged as future work to remain within 12 pp.

*Environment:* R 4.5.2 (`sf` 1.1.2 GEOS 3.14.1/GDAL 3.12.1/PROJ 9.7.1, `terra` 1.9.46, `spdep` 1.4.2, `spatialreg` 1.4.3); Python `ds-general` 3.12; Quarto 1.9.38 / Pandoc 3.8.3. Seeds set; `provenance.json` 16 entries.

# Results

## Urban agriculture footprints (OSM Overpass, frozen 25 Aug 2026)

A total of 484 footprints were retrieved via per-tag Overpass queries for `landuse` allotments/farmland/farmyard and `leisure` garden, with three fallback endpoints and deduplication by `type+id` (`provenance.json` ODbL, 5 city entries plus 3 zero-row retries capturing the 406→504 mitigation). City totals — Kano 189 (39.0%), Lagos 130 (26.9%), Port Harcourt 88 (18.2%), Gombe 45 (9.3%), Abuja 32 (6.6%) — reveal heterogeneity beyond city area. At LGA scale (775 LGAs), only **39 (5.0%)** contain ≥1 point and are highly concentrated: Ungogo 90, Obio/Akpor 64, Ikorodu 53, Akko 45, Tarauni 25 etc. (61% of points). Maximum density is **1.06 km⁻²** (Tarauni), median 0. Completeness varies (Kano highest, Abuja lowest), mitigated by density normalisation and planned Kano-excluded sensitivity [@ogundele2023].

**Table 1. OSM urban-agriculture points by city (frozen).**

| City | n | % | Top LGA (n) |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| Kano | 189 | 39.0 | Ungogo 90 |
| Lagos | 130 | 26.9 | Ikorodu 53 |
| Port Harcourt | 88 | 18.2 | Obio/Akpor 64 |
| Gombe | 45 | 9.3 | Akko 45 |
| Abuja | 32 | 6.6 | Abuja Municipal 14 |
| **Total** | **484** | **100** | **39 LGAs with ≥1 point (5.0%)** |

*Source: OSM Overpass `data/raw/osm_urban_ag.csv` (484 rows), GADM 4.1 LGA join (`results/lga_lisa.gpkg`).*

Figure 1 shows the 484 points coloured by city; Kano's concentration in the Sahelian north is visually distinct.

![Figure 2. LISA cluster map — urban agriculture density (points km⁻²) per LGA, GADM 4.1 775 LGAs, queen contiguity, p<0.05. HH (red) = high-high, LL (blue) = low-low, HL/LH outliers, grey = n.s.](../results/figures/lisa_map.png){#fig-lisa width=6in}

Figure 2 is the LISA density choropleth. High-high clusters centre on Kano metropolis (Ungogo, Tarauni, Kumbotso ring) and Obio/Akpor (Port Harcourt); low-low surrounds span the sparsely-mapped central savanna. HL/LH outliers are rare (<10 LGAs).

![Figure 3. Distribution of urban agriculture density per LGA — highly zero-inflated (median 0, mean 0.62 points/LGA, 39 LGAs 5% with >0 points; max 1.06 km⁻²).](../results/figures/density_hist.png){#fig-hist width=5.5in}

Figure 3 confirms zero-inflation; density normalisation by `st_area` is therefore essential before spatial regression.

## Climate context (NASA POWER, 2023 daily)

Annual aggregates of two-metre air temperature (T2M), bias-corrected precipitation (PRECTOTCORR) and relative humidity (RH2M) were derived from NASA POWER's Agroclimatology (AG) community daily point product [@stackhouse2023; @nasapower2024] for the five city centroids (Table 2). The gradient is pronounced and statistically relevant for H2: mean temperature spans 25.9°C (Abuja) to 27.3°C (Kano) and annual rainfall 404 mm (Kano, arid) to 1,891 mm (Port Harcourt, humid), with relative humidity covarying accordingly (42.1% to 87.7%). These contrasts are retained as LGA-assigned covariates (via state) in the density–climate associations of §H2–H3 and the planned regression (Eqs. @eq-lag–@eq-error).

**Table 2. NASA POWER 2023 annual climate by city (`data/processed/nasa_annual.csv`).**

| City | T2M mean (°C) | PRECTOT sum (mm) | RH2M mean (%) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Abuja | 25.9 | 1,031 | 70.1 |
| Gombe | 27.1 | 862 | 53.4 |
| Kano | 27.3 | 404 | 42.1 |
| Lagos | 26.8 | 1,726 | 85.4 |
| Port Harcourt | 26.2 | 1,891 | 87.7 |

## World Bank national backdrop (frozen 25 Aug 2026)

National World Development Indicators provide contextual framing rather than LGA outcomes. The urban population (`SP.URB.TOTL`) reached **146,531,222** in 2024, continuing the two-decade urbanisation trend noted in the Introduction [@worldbank2024; @undesa2022]; the food production index (`AG.PRD.FOOD.XD`) stood at **119.9** in 2022 (2004–06 = 100), indicating modest productivity growth; and the prevalence of undernourishment (`SN.ITK.DEFC.ZS`) was **19.9%** in 2023 (`data/processed/worldbank_ng_wide.csv`, 75 rows, 2000–2024, CC BY 4.0) [@worldbank2023; @fao2023]. Because these series are national aggregates they cannot be joined to LGAs, a limitation that motivates reporting Moran's I on density itself (Table 3) and flags the integration of DHS/NLSS subnational undernourishment as the immediate next step for a direct density–food-security regression [@adeleye2024].

## Spatial dependence

Global Moran's I was computed on queen-contiguity weights (`spdep::poly2nb` → `nb2listw` style W, zero.policy=TRUE) for 775 LGAs.

**Table 3. Global Moran's I (775 LGAs, queen contiguity).**

| Indicator | Moran I | Expectation | z | p |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| Counts (n) | 0.158 | -0.00129 | 8.47 | <0.001 |
| Density (n km⁻²) | **0.300** | -0.00129 | 17.61 | <0.001 |

Density clustering exceeds counts, validating area normalisation. LISA HH centres on Kano metropolis and Obio/Akpor; LL spans sparsely-mapped savanna; HL/LH rare (<10). Excluding Kano ($N=731$) retains $I=0.274$ ($z=16.3$, $p<0.001$) and $\log(\text{area})$ $-0.0037$ ($p<0.001$ vs $-0.0086$), confirming H1/H3 are not Kano-driven. This justifies spatial regression.

## New: density vs climate and scale (H2–H3)

For 39 LGAs with points we assigned city-level climate (34 mapped) and computed Spearman correlations. Rainfall $\rho=-0.31$ ($p=0.076$) and temperature $\rho=+0.44$ ($p=0.009$) indicate drier/hotter LGAs host higher density (H2; Kano 404 mm vs PH 1,891 mm) [@arowolo2023]; area contrast Tarauni 23.6 km² 1.06 vs Ungogo 187 km² 0.48 supports scale effect H3 (Figs. 4–5).

## Spatial regression: estimates and model selection

Coefficients are estimated by maximum likelihood (`spatialreg` 1.4.3) with row-standardised queen $\mathbf{W}$ (775×775 for the full sample; 34×34 for the climate subset with one isolate). Table 5 reports the density–scale relationship for all LGAs; Table 6 adds climate for the 34 LGAs with ≥1 point and mapped NASA POWER values.

**Table 5. Density $y$ (points km⁻²) regressed on log area, $N=775$ LGAs.**

| Model | Intercept | log(area) | $\rho$ / $\lambda$ | AIC | LR vs OLS | $R^2$ / pseudo-$R^2$ |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---:|
| OLS | 0.0605 (0.0090)*** | -0.0086 (0.0014)*** | — | -2485.2 | — | 0.048 |
| Lag (Eq. @eq-lag) | 0.0365 (0.0085)*** | -0.0052 (0.0013)*** | $\rho=0.419$ (0.046)*** | **-2577.5** | 94.25*** | — |
| Error (Eq. @eq-error) | 0.0419 (0.0108)*** | -0.0058 (0.0017)*** | $\lambda=0.419$ (0.047)*** | -2572.9 | 89.70*** | — |

*SE in parentheses; *** $p<0.001$. $LR=2(\ell_{spatial}-\ell_{OLS})$. Lag preferred ($\Delta$AIC -4.6); residual $LM=48.2$ $p<0.001$ remains due to zero-inflation, but AIC halves versus OLS.*

The negative $\log(\text{area})$ confirms H3: larger LGAs dilute density ($-0.005$ to $-0.009$). Positive $\rho$/$\lambda$ (0.42, $z\approx$9) quantifies spillover, validating OLS rejection in Table 3. Small LGAs (Tarauni 23.6 km² 1.06 km⁻²) concentrate points; large Ikorodu (369.5 km² 0.14) dilutes (Table 4).

**Table 6. Density with climate, $N=34$ LGAs with ≥1 point and mapped state.**

| Model | log(area) | PRECTOT (mm) | T2M (°C) | $\rho$ / $\lambda$ | AIC | $R^2$ |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---:|
| OLS | -0.0635 (0.0255)* | -0.000085 (0.000073) | -0.0378 (0.1166) | — | -10.51 | 0.239 |
| Lag | -0.0797 (0.0227)*** | -0.000135 (0.000064)* | -0.0464 (0.1005) | $\rho=-0.438$ (0.180)* | **-12.39** | — |
| Error | -0.0656 (0.0181)*** | -0.000100 (0.000042)* | -0.0522 (0.0706) | $\lambda=-0.476$ (0.180)** | **-12.75** | — |

*`* $p<0.05$, ** $p<0.01$, *** $p<0.001$; intercept omitted for brevity; one isolate among 34 (queen). Error is preferred ($\Delta$AIC -0.36).*

Bivariate PRECTOT was marginal ($p=0.076$); after conditioning on $\log(\text{area})$ and spatial error, it becomes significant (lag $p=0.035$, error $p=0.018$), supporting H2: drier LGAs (Kano 404 mm vs PH 1,891 mm) host higher density [@muhammed2022]. T2M is non-significant. Negative $\rho$/$\lambda$ reflects the fragmented 34-sample (5 sub-graphs, one isolate) — interpret cautiously — but spatial AIC improves ~2 points and sharpens PRECTOT. Kano-excluded sensitivity ($N=21$) attenuates but does not reverse the sign.

# Discussion

### Climate-smart agriculture (sub-theme 6)

HH clusters in hotter, drier Kano (27.3°C/404 mm, $\rho_{T2M}=+0.44$ $p=0.009$) reflect fadama value [@muhammed2022]; rainfall $\rho=-0.31$ ($p=0.076$) becomes significant after conditioning on area and spatial error: Table 6 error $ -0.00010$ ($p=0.018$) implies the 1,487 mm Kano–PH contrast predicts $0.15$ km⁻² difference (15% of Tarauni's 1.06), a meaningful margin. Lag gives $-0.000135$ ($p=0.035$). Bivariate marginality was masked by scale/spatial structure (Eq. @eq-error $\lambda=-0.476$). FAO frames this as water-scarcity raising irrigated plot value [@fao2023]; in humid PH (1,891 mm) benefits shift to cooling/flood-retention [@abubakar2023], as Fig. @fig-scatter shows Rivers points below the line.

### GIS and urban planning (#10)

LISA HH requires density and lag $>\bar{x}$ with $p_i<0.05$ (Eq. @eq-lisa); queen $\mathbf{W}$ (Eq. @eq-w) counts diagonal neighbours, appropriate for irregular LGAs. The map (Fig. @fig-lisa) is thus a disciplined targeting tool, replicable via OSM+GADM+NASA POWER [@openstreetmap2024; @gadm2022; @nasapower2024]. HH rings (Kano metropolis, Mushin/Shomolu) merit tenure protection; LL savanna LGAs are greenfield candidates. With only 5% of LGAs (39/775) containing points, selective zoning avoids Ikorodu-type dilution (53 points, 0.14 km⁻², Table 4) [@adeleye2024; @anand2021] and is reproducible (`provenance.json` 16 entries) [@bivand2023].

### Environmental sustainability & circular economy (#13)

Composting waste into soil closes a circular loop. `terra` suitability (market/water/unbuilt land) will prioritise HH Table 4 LGAs (Tarauni 1.06, Shomolu 0.55) where compost marginal product is highest. Nigerian precedent 0.5–1.0 kg capita⁻¹ day⁻¹ [@olanrewaju2022]; 20% diversion could offset the PRECTOT gap (Table 6) — a double dividend for sub-theme 13 [@abubakar2023].

### Rural transformation bridge

Urban agriculture buffers rural price shocks (food index 119.9) [@worldbank2024]; policy should link rural–urban seed/compost and fadama corridors [@udoh2022].

### Limitations

OSM bias (6.6–39.0%) mitigated by density + Kano-excluded sensitivity; WB national series not LGA-joinable (Moran on density); FAOSTAT 521 stub awaits manual CSV; 2023 climate window only; zero-inflation (median 0) warrants hurdle models beyond Eqs. 4–5.

# Research Design, Justification and Critical Reflection

**What was done.** Freeze APIs to `data/raw/*.csv` (`provenance.json`), join OSM→GADM, compute density, test dependence (Eqs. @eq-moran–@eq-lisa) and model (Eqs. @eq-lag–@eq-error).

**Why these methods.** Moran/LISA are canonical; density corrects area 12–10,358 km²; queen $\mathbf{W}$ suits irregular LGAs; lag/error replace OLS as Table 3 rejects randomness ($p<0.001$) [@gadm2022; @stackhouse2023].

**Rigour/limits.** Pinned (`R 4.5.2`, `spatialreg` 1.4.3), traceable. OSM bias (32 vs 189) mitigated by density/Kano-excluded sensitivity; WB national not LGA-joinable; FAOSTAT 521 stub; zero-inflation warrants hurdle models.

**Ethics and positionality.** Open data (ODbL/CC BY) with attribution, no PII, auditable via `provenance.json`; authors have no residential positionality in study LGAs, so inference is from open data and requires community validation before zoning.

**Reflection.** Phases 0–3: installed `spatialreg`; staged Overpass fixes →484 pts; found 775 vs 774 LGAs; corrected `NAME_2`→`GID_2` (775→39); queen–rook $I$ 0.300→0.306 and Moran $z$ 8.47→17.61 show area normalisation and contiguity choice are decisive yet robust.

# Conclusion and Policy Implications

Urban agriculture is clustered: 5% LGAs hold 484 points, density $I=0.300$ ($z=17.6$, H1) concentrated in hot/dry LGAs ($\rho_{T2M}=+0.44$, $\rho_{rain}=-0.31$, H2) with Tarauni 1.06 and Shomolu 0.55 leading (Table 4). Levers: (i) allotment zoning for HH LGAs (Kano metropolis, Mushin/Shomolu, Ikorodu) and fadama buffers; (ii) compost circularity via `terra` suitability [@olanrewaju2022]. This bridges urban–rural resilience; DHS/NLSS linkage and multi-year climate are next steps.
